Week 21 Appendix: Pressure Without Rupture

Immigration raids, troop deployments, and a senator's forcible removal met fierce court resistance, leaving the clock's needle nearly still.

This was a high-pressure week for democratic structure, defined by the fusion of aggressive immigration enforcement, military-style domestic deployment, retaliation against oversight, and escalating information control. The most consequential pattern was the use of federal force and emergency-style authority in Los Angeles: ICE raids, mass arrests, National Guard federalization over California’s objection, Marine deployment, and rhetoric portraying protest and migration as invasion or insurrection. That cluster strongly worsened traits tied to unchecked executive power, weaponized law, suppression of dissent, militarized governance, and federal punishment of disfavored jurisdictions. A second major theme was institutional retaliation: members of Congress were denied access to detention sites, Senator Padilla was forcibly removed and handcuffed, and DOJ actions targeted political speech and elected officials. A third theme was ideological capture of state capacity, visible in the purge and replacement of vaccine advisers, attacks on universities and public broadcasters, censorship pressures in education and culture, and manipulation or suppression of official information. Courts provided some meaningful resistance, especially on elections, immigration due process, and troop deployment, but the week’s raw structural force still ran heavily toward authoritarian entrenchment.
